title: Cargo Door Latch Shaft Assembly — Removal

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of one cargo door latch shaft assembly with its bearing bushes, including the end float measurement that has to be recorded before the shaft is withdrawn.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of one latch shaft assembly from a cargo door, together with the bearing bushes and the retaining hardware.
sections.job_setup_note: The cargo door must be in the maintenance position with the door support strut fitted and the door control system isolated. The end float measurement has to be taken before anything is disturbed, because the installation task shims the warning sensor target to the measured value. Work is from inside the compartment and the latch access panels must be removed first.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: FIT THE DOOR SUPPORT STRUT AND ISOLATE THE DOOR CONTROL SYSTEM BEFORE YOU REMOVE ANY LATCH COMPONENT. THE DOOR CAN MOVE UNDER ITS OWN WEIGHT. 2. Remove the latch access panels from inside the compartment. 3. Measure the shaft end float with the dial gauge and record the value on the work card. 4. Disconnect the latch actuator link at the shaft crank. 5. Remove the lockwire and the retaining hardware at each bearing position. 6. CAUTION: SUPPORT THE SHAFT AT BOTH ENDS WHILE IT IS WITHDRAWN. AN UNSUPPORTED SHAFT CAN DAMAGE THE BEARING BORE. 7. Withdraw the shaft from the outboard end and put it on the padded support. 8. Remove the retaining angle D5230139019163 by drilling out the blind rivets EN989730K5 and the swaged collars LN181939-7B. 9. Press the bearing bushes out of the latch stiffener D5230135108629 using the extraction adapter. 10. Examine the bore for scoring, ovality and fretting, and record the measured bore diameter at three positions. 11. Bag and identify the removed items.
sections.close_out: Make sure that no swarf remains in the latch cavity and that the bore is protected against damage until the installation task starts. Record the end float, the bore measurements and the condition of the removed bushes in the aircraft technical record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. On aircraft post the self-lubricating bush standard the bushes are removed as a set of four.

safety_precautions: Fit the door support strut before any latch component is removed.
Isolate the cargo door control system and put the warning notices in position.
Do not stand below the door while the latch shaft is withdrawn.
